title: Felix and the Hollow
premise: Silas Pemberton survives in the Hollow, a valley where magic cannot follow, by stealing memories and selling them to the desperate. When the old gods resume answering prayers, a dying knight drags Silas out of the valley with a stolen memory of King Aldric — a memory proving the king was hollowed out years ago and replaced by something wearing his crown. Hunted by the god-touched Inquisition and shadowed by Wren, an orphan girl whose memories he once stole, Silas must gather three relics of the old gods to unbind the true king before the impostor completes a rite that will silence every god forever. At the rite's climax Silas learns the impostor is the echo of his own stolen childhood memory given flesh, and he can only destroy it by surrendering the last memory of his mother — the price of survival finally come due. He pays it, frees Aldric, and returns to the Hollow hollowed himself, where Wren and the found family he built give him new memories worth keeping.
about_author: Cyrus Lockridge is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging letters from people begging gods for miracles. He writes fantasy about what people trade away to survive, and lives somewhere with poor cell reception.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Silas Pemberton lifts a widow's grief from her mind and sells it back to her as peace, establishing the Hollow's economy of stolen memories. His POV; wry, detached. The beat: comfort purchased at moral cost, and Silas's careful refusal to feel anything about it.

chapters.title: A Knock at the Wrong Door
chapters.summary: Wren, the orphan whose childhood memories Silas sold years ago, arrives demanding answers about her past. His POV; guilt surfacing. The beat: the first crack in Silas's armor — she remembers nothing but knows something was taken.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: For the first time in living memory, a shrine in the Hollow flickers with divine light; the old gods are answering again. Wren's POV; wonder curdling into fear. The beat: the impossible made visible, and the valley's protection beginning to fail.

chapters.title: The Knight Who Fell From the Sky
chapters.summary: A mortally wounded knight crashes at the valley's edge clutching a sealed memory-vial. Silas's POV; reluctant heroism. The beat: duty arriving uninvited — the knight dies whispering 'the crown is empty.'

chapters.title: What the Vial Showed
chapters.summary: Inside the vial: a memory of King Aldric being hollowed out by a thing of smoke and borrowed faces. Silas's POV; horror. The beat: knowledge as burden — now Silas can't unknow, and the Inquisition will kill anyone who knows.

chapters.title: Inquisition at the Border
chapters.summary: God-touched inquisitors seal the valley's passes, hunting the vial. Wren's POV; terror and defiance. The beat: the safe valley becomes a trap, forcing the choice between hiding and running.

chapters.title: Leaving the Hollow
chapters.summary: Silas smuggles Wren and the vial through a smuggler's tunnel, leaving the only place magic can't touch him. His POV; fear of exposure. The beat: crossing the threshold — outside, his own stolen memories begin whispering to him.

chapters.title: The Road of Small Gods
chapters.summary: Traveling toward the capital, they pass villages where minor gods grant crude miracles for terrible prices. Wren's POV; moral vertigo. The beat: the world's rules revealed — divinity has returned hungry, not kind.

chapters.title: The Thief's Guild Remembers Him
chapters.summary: Silas seeks his old fence, Marlow, in the river city of Casterhale, but Marlow owes the Inquisition favors. Silas's POV; paranoia. The beat: betrayal foreshadowed — every ally has a price, including Silas.

chapters.title: Bargain With a Drowned God
chapters.summary: To learn the first relic's location, Silas trades a stolen memory to a river god. His POV; self-loss. The beat: the cost made physical — he can no longer recall his mother's face, only that he had one.

chapters.title: The Relic in the Bell Tower
chapters.summary: The first relic, a god's tongue-bone, hangs in a haunted bell tower guarded by a priest gone mad with answered prayers. Wren's POV; courage under pressure. The beat: Wren saves Silas, reversing their debt and forging real trust.

chapters.title: Marlow's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marlow sells their route to the Inquisition; the pair barely escape Casterhale burning behind them. Silas's POV; rage and resignation. The beat: loyalty tested — Silas nearly abandons Wren to save himself, and hates that he considered it.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor Vess
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Vess, introduced in her own POV, interrogates Marlow and reveals she hunts the vial because she once prayed and was answered horribly. Her POV; chilling sympathy. The beat: the antagonist humanized — she believes she's saving the world from gods.

chapters.title: Hollowed Men
chapters.summary: They find a village where everyone smiles identically — the impostor king's agents have begun hollowing whole towns. Silas's POV; dread. The beat: stakes escalate from personal survival to civilizational erasure.

chapters.title: The Second Relic's Keeper
chapters.summary: The second relic, a god's eye-stone, is held by a blind oracle who demands a memory of love as payment. Wren's POV; sacrifice. The beat: Wren offers her one good memory of Silas, choosing their future over her past.

chapters.title: Visions Paid For
chapters.summary: The eye-stone shows them the rite: on midwinter night, the impostor will bind all gods' names into the crown and unmake them. Silas's POV; urgency. The beat: the clock starts — six weeks until midwinter, and the capital is a thousand miles away.

chapters.title: Riding With Pilgrims
chapters.summary: They join a pilgrim caravan heading to the capital for the king's midwinter blessing. Ensemble feel via alternating close-third; cautious hope. The beat: found family begins forming among strangers who share their road and their fear.

chapters.title: The Boy Named Tam
chapters.summary: A pilgrim boy, Tam, attaches himself to Silas, convinced the thief is a hero from a story. Silas's POV; tenderness resisted. The beat: Silas becomes, against his will, someone worth imitating.

chapters.title: Checkpoint of Ash
chapters.summary: An Inquisition checkpoint forces the pilgrims to surrender memories; Silas must steal them back without being caught. His POV; high tension. The beat: skill showcased under pressure, and Vess glimpses his face.

chapters.title: Vess Offers a Deal
chapters.summary: Vess corners Silas privately: help her kill the impostor king and she'll let Wren go. His POV; temptation. The beat: the devil's bargain — her goal matches his, but her method requires sacrificing the pilgrims as bait.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Silas refuses Vess; she takes Tam hostage as insurance. Wren's POV; fury and fear. The beat: the theme sharpened — truth (Vess's cause is just) versus loyalty (they won't spend children to win).

chapters.title: Rescue at the Shrine of Teeth
chapters.summary: A night raid frees Tam from the shrine where Vess holds him, using the tongue-bone relic to command the shrine's guardian. Silas's POV; desperation and daring. The beat: victory with wounds — Silas is marked by the guardian's curse.

chapters.title: The Curse's Whisper
chapters.summary: The guardian's curse lets Silas hear the impostor king's thoughts across distance — and the king hears his. Alternating POV; psychological horror. The beat: hunter and hunted linked; the impostor speaks to Silas in his mother's voice.

chapters.title: The Impostor's Truth
chapters.summary: Through the link, Silas learns the impostor is grown from a discarded memory — his own, stolen long ago by the man who taught him theft. Silas's POV; devastating recognition. The beat: the enemy is himself, orphaned and weaponized.

chapters.title: Confession by Firelight
chapters.summary: Silas confesses everything to Wren: that he stole her memories, that the monster hunting them is made from his past. Wren's POV; heartbreak and grace. The beat: truth offered freely for the first time — and accepted.

chapters.title: The Capital of Bells
chapters.summary: They reach the capital mid-festival, its bells tuned to suppress divine voices. Silas's POV; claustrophobic awe. The beat: entering the lion's den disguised as pilgrims, relics hidden in a beggar's cart.

chapters.title: The Court of the Hollow King
chapters.summary: Using stolen court memories as currency, Silas buys an audience with the king and sees the emptiness behind the crown up close. His POV; cold horror. The beat: confirmation — and the discovery that the third relic lies beneath the palace.

chapters.title: The God Beneath the Palace
chapters.summary: The third relic, a god's heart, is buried in the palace crypt, kept as the impostor's anchor. Wren's POV; grave-robbing suspense. The beat: they take the heart, and the palace wakes screaming.

chapters.title: Alarm in the Dark
chapters.summary: Fleeing the crypt, they're cut off; Tam is captured by royal guards while covering their escape. Silas's POV; guilt like a blade. The beat: the cost of the mission lands on the innocent — Silas's found family bleeding for him.

chapters.title: Prisoners of the Crown
chapters.summary: Tam is brought before the impostor, who reads the boy's memories to find Silas. Tam's POV; bravery beyond his years. The beat: the child refuses to break, buying time and shaming the monster.

chapters.title: Vess's Crisis of Faith
chapters.summary: Vess witnesses the impostor hollowing Tam and realizes her Inquisition serves the very thing she feared. Her POV; faith shattered. The beat: the antagonist turns — she chooses truth over orders.

chapters.title: Uneasy Alliance
chapters.summary: Vess breaks Tam out and delivers him to Silas with a map of the rite chamber and no apology. Silas's POV; wary truce. The beat: enemies becoming allies because the truth outranks old grievances.

chapters.title: Midwinter Eve
chapters.summary: Preparations: the three relics assembled, the plan laid, farewells spoken in case none return. Ensemble; quiet dread. The beat: the calm before — each character naming what they're willing to lose.

chapters.title: The Rite Begins
chapters.summary: Midwinter night: the impostor starts binding the gods' names into the crown as the sky above the capital goes dark. Alternating POV; apocalyptic scale. The beat: the world holding its breath.

chapters.title: Storming the Rite Chamber
chapters.summary: Silas, Wren, Vess, and Tam fight through the hollowed guard to reach the dais. Silas's POV; ferocious momentum. The beat: every ally spends themselves fully — found family as a weapon.

chapters.title: Face to Face With Himself
chapters.summary: Silas confronts the impostor, who offers him a kingdom built from shared memory if he'll walk away. Silas's POV; the darkest temptation. The beat: the final test of the theme — survival offered at the price of everyone else.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Silas feeds the impostor his mother's memory — the original seed — starving it even as Wren and Vess complete the unbinding with the relics. Multiple POV; sacrificial climax. The beat: the price of survival paid in full; the true Aldric reawakens weeping.

chapters.title: After the Silence
chapters.summary: The gods withdraw, sated or satisfied; Aldric, restored but broken, abdicates rather than rule over what was done in his name. Wren's POV; exhausted dawn. The beat: victory without triumph — the cost tallied honestly.

chapters.title: Memories Worth Keeping
chapters.summary: Silas, hollowed by his sacrifice, returns to the valley with Wren, Tam, and Vess, who begin giving him their memories of him freely. Silas's POV; bittersweet warmth. The beat: found family rebuilding what was lost — memory as gift, not theft.

chapters.title: The Hollow, No Longer Empty
chapters.summary: Epilogue: seasons later, the valley's shrines stay dark but its houses are full; Silas keeps a shop that returns memories instead of taking them. His POV; hard-won peace. The beat: resolution — loyalty and truth reconciled, survival finally worth its price.
